narrative_vs_numbers.summary: TCS management demonstrated high predictability on deal flow and cost impacts, beating full-year order book expectations with $40.7B in TCV against an expected US$38- 39 billion, while accurately forecasting Q1 FY27 wage hike headwinds at 170 bps within the guided 150 to 200 basis points range. However, sequential margin recovery stalled in Q2 FY27 at 24% as operational leverage was offset by strategic reinvestments in subcontractors and talent, trailing the aspirational 25% plus exit trajectory.

guided.guidance: Management stated an intention to inch up through the quarter and aim to exit at 25% plus.
guided.source: Q1 FY27 Concall Transcript (15-Jul-2026), PDF p. 23 — "Ashwin, usually, we take a big headwind upfront in Q1, and we inch up through the quarter. We want to exit at 25% plus"

delivered.actual: Operating margins remained stable sequentially at 24%.
delivered.source: Q2 FY27 Concall Transcript (14-Oct-2026), PDF p. 5 — "Our operating margins remained stable sequentially at 24%. Consistent with our philosophy to drive long-term profitable growth, we continued to prioritize investments for growth."

quarters.commentary: Operating margins remained flat sequentially at 24% instead of expanding toward the aspirational 25% plus level, driven by deliberate investments in niche talent and subcontractor costs.

guided.guidance: Management guided that the impact of wage increments would be in the range of 150 to 200 basis points.
guided.source: Q4 FY26 Concall Transcript (14-Apr-2026), PDF p. 30 — "what we have seen in the past annual increment cycle, which had been in the range of 150 to 200 basis points."

delivered.actual: Annual increments for the global workforce impacted margins by 170 bps.
delivered.source: Q1 FY27 Concall Transcript (15-Jul-2026), PDF p. 5 — "In Q1, we rolled out annual increments for our global workforce, which impacted margins by 170 bps."

quarters.commentary: The operating margin impact from global workforce wage increments landed at 170 bps, well within management's prior projected band of 150 to 200 basis points.

guided.guidance: Management stated that the order book would be somewhere closer to about US$38- 39 billion for the year.
guided.source: Q3 FY26 Concall Transcript (16-Jan-2026), PDF p. 27 — "If this trend continues, we will be somewhere closer to about US$38- 39 billion for the year, which will be one of the highest."

delivered.actual: TCS delivered a strong $40.7B in TCV including 5 mega deals.
delivered.source: Q4 FY26 Concall Transcript (14-Apr-2026), PDF p. 5 — "we delivered a strong $40.7B in TCV including 5 mega deals. We maintained a strong focus on execution"

quarters.commentary: Full-year order book closed at $40.7B in TCV supported by 5 mega deals, outperforming management's prior run-rate expectation of US$38- 39 billion.

narrative_vs_numbers.pattern: Management routinely delivers or beats on large deal conversions and models labor cost cycles accurately, but consistently absorbs margin upside by reinvesting operational tailwinds into bench capacity and strategic capabilities.
